headline: Spanish Cognates Master
threshold: Use familiar Spanish-English word families without trusting spelling alone. Practice pronunciation, stress, agreement and false friends through contextual reading and original responses.

lessons.title: Resolve a hotel reservation
lessons.objective: Resolve a hotel reservation: Similar spelling is a useful clue, not proof of meaning.

words.es: Busco un hotel cerca del hospital.
words.en: I am looking for a hotel near the hospital.

words.es: Pregunto si aceptan un animal pequeño.
words.en: I ask whether they accept a small animal.

words.es: La radio está en la habitación.
words.en: The radio is in the room.
I review the plan for tomorrow.

words.es: En recepción explico que falta una noche en la reserva.
words.en: At reception I explain that one night is missing from the reservation.

words.es: La persona busca una habitación disponible.
words.en: The person looks for an available room.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing resolve a hotel reservation. Similar spelling is a useful clue, not proof of meaning. Check the whole sentence and say Spanish vowels clearly. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Similar spelling is a useful clue, not proof of meaning. Check the whole sentence and say Spanish vowels clearly.

examples.es: Busco un hotel cerca del hospital.
examples.en: I am looking for a hotel near the hospital.

examples.es: Una persona confirma mi reserva.
examples.en: A person confirms my reservation.

lessons.title: Explain a journey from two notices

lessons.focus: Explain a journey from two notices

words.en: I need information about the station.

words.es: La dirección está en el mensaje.
words.en: The address is in the message.

words.es: Una conversación con Ana aclara la situación.
words.en: A conversation with Ana clarifies the situation.

words.es: La organización ofrece clases de educación para adultos.
words.en: The organization offers adult education classes.

words.es: La comunicación por teléfono es clara.
Anoto la información y confirmo la dirección.
words.en: I write down the information and confirm the address.

words.es: En el andén hay otra información sobre la salida.
words.en: On the platform there is more information about the departure.

words.es: Compruebo el destino que aparece en mi billete.
words.en: I check the destination shown on my ticket.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing explain a journey from two notices. Many English -tion nouns have a related Spanish -ción form. Learn each word with its meaning; the written accent marks stress. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Many English -tion nouns have a related Spanish -ción form. Learn each word with its meaning; the written accent marks stress.

examples.es: Necesito información sobre la estación.

examples.es: La dirección está en el mensaje.

lessons.title: Defend a group decision
lessons.objective: Defend a group decision: Related English -sion nouns often end in Spanish -sión.

words.es: Tenemos una sesión para elegir un programa de televisión.
words.en: We have a session to choose a television program.

words.es: La versión nueva incluye una revisión del horario.
words.en: The new version includes a review of the schedule.

words.es: La decisión depende del tiempo disponible.
words.en: The decision depends on the available time.

words.es: Esta ocasión permite escuchar opiniones distintas.
words.en: This occasion allows us to hear different opinions.

words.es: Nuestra conclusión es probar la versión corta.
words.en: Our conclusion is to try the short version.

words.es: Cada opinión tiene un argumento que merece atención.
words.en: Each opinion has an argument that deserves attention.

words.es: Una persona pide más tiempo para revisar la versión nueva.
words.en: A person asks for more time to review the new version.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing defend a group decision. Related English -sion nouns often end in Spanish -sión. Double consonants and accents do not always match; check the actual word. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Related English -sion nouns often end in Spanish -sión. Double consonants and accents do not always match; check the actual word.

examples.es: Tenemos una sesión para elegir un programa de televisión.
examples.en: We have a session to choose a television program.

examples.en: The new version includes a review of the schedule.

lessons.title: Present a community proposal
lessons.objective: Present a community proposal: Many English -ity nouns correspond to Spanish -idad or -dad nouns.

words.es: La universidad prepara una actividad para la comunidad.
words.en: The university is preparing an activity for the community.

words.es: Hay una posibilidad de participar el sábado.
words.en: There is a possibility of participating on Saturday.
In fact, we need more volunteers.

words.es: La necesidad principal es mejorar la calidad del servicio.
words.en: The main need is to improve the quality of the service.

words.es: Una tarjeta confirma la identidad de cada participante.
words.en: A card confirms each participant's identity.

words.es: La comunidad decide repetir la actividad.
words.en: The community decides to repeat the activity.

words.es: Nuestra propuesta tiene un objetivo concreto para el barrio.
words.en: Our proposal has a specific goal for the neighborhood.

words.es: El presupuesto permite pagar material, pero no todo el servicio.
words.en: The budget allows us to pay for materials, but not the whole service.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing present a community proposal. Many English -ity nouns correspond to Spanish -idad or -dad nouns. These nouns are usually feminine; learn la with the word. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Many English -ity nouns correspond to Spanish -idad or -dad nouns. These nouns are usually feminine; learn la with the word.

examples.es: La universidad prepara una actividad para la comunidad.
examples.en: The university is preparing an activity for the community.

examples.es: Hay una posibilidad de participar el sábado.
examples.en: There is a possibility of participating on Saturday.

lessons.title: Teach a routine without translating every word
lessons.objective: Teach a routine without translating every word: Many Spanish -mente adverbs relate to English -ly forms.
lessons.focus: Teach a routine without translating every word

words.en: I normally arrive at class early.

words.es: Generalmente leo lentamente la primera página.
words.en: I generally read the first page slowly.

words.es: La profesora explica claramente el ejemplo.
words.en: The teacher explains the example clearly.
I especially practice the new words.

words.es: No repito exactamente el mismo ejemplo.
words.en: I do not repeat exactly the same example.

words.es: Mi compañera necesita una pausa antes de dar su respuesta.
words.en: My classmate needs a pause before giving her answer.

words.es: Cambio el ritmo y explico un detalle con otro ejemplo.
words.en: I change the pace and explain one detail with another example.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing teach a routine without translating every word. Many Spanish -mente adverbs relate to English -ly forms. The adjective base may change; similar-looking adverbs can still differ in meaning. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Many Spanish -mente adverbs relate to English -ly forms. The adjective base may change; similar-looking adverbs can still differ in meaning.

examples.es: Normalmente llego a clase temprano.
examples.en: I normally arrive at class early.

examples.es: Generalmente leo lentamente la primera página.
examples.en: I generally read the first page slowly.

lessons.title: Describe a visitor respectfully
lessons.objective: Describe a visitor respectfully: English -ous adjectives often have Spanish relatives in -oso.

words.es: Nuestro grupo visita un museo famoso.
words.en: Our group visits a famous museum.

words.es: Un niño curioso hace una pregunta.
words.en: A curious child asks a question.

words.es: Un vecino generoso paga la visita.
words.en: A generous neighbor pays for the visit.

words.es: Al principio estoy nervioso porque no conozco al grupo.
words.en: At first I am nervous because I do not know the group.

words.es: El guía dice que ese camino es peligroso.
words.en: The guide says that path is dangerous.

words.es: Al final compartimos un almuerzo delicioso.
words.en: At the end we share a delicious lunch.

words.es: La guía pregunta qué impresión nos deja la visita.
words.en: The guide asks what impression the visit leaves on us.

words.es: Describo al vecino como generoso y al niño como curioso.
words.en: I describe the neighbor as generous and the child as curious.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing describe a visitor respectfully. English -ous adjectives often have Spanish relatives in -oso. Use -osa, -osos or -osas when needed for agreement; this is a clue, not a universal conversion rule. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: English -ous adjectives often have Spanish relatives in -oso. Use -osa, -osos or -osas when needed for agreement; this is a clue, not a universal conversion rule.

examples.es: Nuestro grupo visita un museo famoso.
examples.en: Our group visits a famous museum.

examples.es: Un niño curioso hace una pregunta.
examples.en: A curious child asks a question.

lessons.title: Compare two practical service plans
lessons.objective: Compare two practical service plans: Many English -ic or -ical adjectives have a related Spanish -ico form.

words.es: Buscamos un servicio práctico para el barrio.
words.en: We are looking for a practical service for the neighborhood.

words.es: El transporte público tiene un precio económico.
words.en: Public transportation has an economical price.

words.es: El plan básico incluye una visita al centro médico.
words.en: The basic plan includes a visit to the medical center.

words.es: Un viaje típico dura veinte minutos.
words.en: A typical trip lasts twenty minutes.

words.es: Pregunto si el servicio está disponible hoy.
words.en: I ask whether the service is available today.
We choose the most practical option.

words.es: La comparación muestra una ventaja de cada opción.
words.en: The comparison shows an advantage of each option.

words.es: El coste del plan básico es menor, pero el horario es limitado.
words.en: The cost of the basic plan is lower, but the hours are limited.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing compare two practical service plans. Many English -ic or -ical adjectives have a related Spanish -ico form. Match gender and number, and keep the written accent when the word has one. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Many English -ic or -ical adjectives have a related Spanish -ico form. Match gender and number, and keep the written accent when the word has one.

examples.es: Buscamos un servicio práctico para el barrio.
examples.en: We are looking for a practical service for the neighborhood.

examples.es: El transporte público tiene un precio económico.
examples.en: Public transportation has an economical price.

lessons.title: Negotiate a cultural event schedule
lessons.objective: Negotiate a cultural event schedule: Many English and Spanish adjectives share -al.

words.es: El festival cultural empieza el viernes.
words.en: The cultural festival starts on Friday.

words.es: Una artista local trae material para la clase.
words.en: A local artist brings material for the class.

words.es: Usamos luz natural para ver los colores.
words.en: We use natural light to see the colors.

words.es: Cada persona explica su proyecto personal.
words.en: Each person explains their personal project.

words.es: La información general aparece en la entrada.
words.en: General information appears at the entrance.

words.es: La presentación final es el domingo.
words.en: The final presentation is on Sunday.

words.es: La presentación del proyecto coincide con otra actividad local.
words.en: The project presentation coincides with another local activity.

words.es: Necesitamos un recurso adicional para cambiar el horario.
words.en: We need an additional resource to change the schedule.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing negotiate a cultural event schedule. Many English and Spanish adjectives share -al. Spanish adjectives in -al normally keep the same form for masculine and feminine; add -es for the plural. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Many English and Spanish adjectives share -al. Spanish adjectives in -al normally keep the same form for masculine and feminine; add -es for the plural.

examples.es: El festival cultural empieza el viernes.
examples.en: The cultural festival starts on Friday.

examples.es: Una artista local trae material para la clase.
examples.en: A local artist brings material for the class.

lessons.title: Explain an action plan with familiar verbs
lessons.objective: Explain an action plan with familiar verbs: English -ize words can have Spanish relatives in -izar, but do not invent a verb from a spelling rule.
lessons.focus: Explain an action plan with familiar verbs

words.es: Vamos a organizar una visita al centro.
words.en: We are going to organize a visit to the center.

words.es: Necesito utilizar el calendario para preparar el viaje.
words.en: I need to use the calendar to prepare the trip.

words.es: Antes de reservar, debemos analizar el precio.
words.en: Before reserving, we must analyze the price.

words.es: Quiero confirmar la fecha con Marta.
words.en: I want to confirm the date with Marta.

words.es: El sábado podemos visitar el museo.
words.en: On Saturday we can visit the museum.

words.es: Si cambia el horario, tenemos que cancelar la reserva.
words.en: If the schedule changes, we have to cancel the reservation.

words.es: El calendario muestra una fecha diferente para la reserva.
words.en: The calendar shows a different date for the reservation.

words.es: Envío un mensaje para confirmar el cambio.
words.en: I send a message to confirm the change.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing explain an action plan with familiar verbs. English -ize words can have Spanish relatives in -izar, but do not invent a verb from a spelling rule. Learn the infinitive and a complete example. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: English -ize words can have Spanish relatives in -izar, but do not invent a verb from a spelling rule. Learn the infinitive and a complete example.

examples.es: Vamos a organizar una visita al centro.
examples.en: We are going to organize a visit to the center.

examples.es: Necesito utilizar el calendario para preparar el viaje.
examples.en: I need to use the calendar to prepare the trip.

lessons.title: Correct gender in a public explanation
lessons.objective: Correct gender in a public explanation: A familiar-looking noun still needs its Spanish gender and stress.
lessons.focus: Correct gender in a public explanation

words.es: El programa muestra un mapa del barrio.
words.en: The program shows a map of the neighborhood.

words.es: Hay un problema con el sistema.
words.en: There is a problem with the system.

words.es: Una persona explica el tema en otro idioma.
words.en: A person explains the topic in another language.

words.es: Miro una foto de la entrada.
words.en: I look at a photo of the entrance.

words.es: El mapa confirma dónde está la oficina.
words.en: The map confirms where the office is.

words.es: Resolvemos el problema y guardamos la foto.
words.en: We solve the problem and save the photo.

words.es: El equipo necesita una solución para el problema del sistema.
words.en: The team needs a solution to the system problem.

words.es: En mi mensaje escribo la versión correcta del programa.
words.en: In my message I write the correct version of the program.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing correct gender in a public explanation. A familiar-looking noun still needs its Spanish gender and stress. El problema and el sistema are masculine despite ending in -a; do not infer meaning or gender from spelling alone. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: A familiar-looking noun still needs its Spanish gender and stress. El problema and el sistema are masculine despite ending in -a; do not infer meaning or gender from spelling alone.

examples.es: El programa muestra un mapa del barrio.
examples.en: The program shows a map of the neighborhood.

examples.es: Hay un problema con el sistema.
examples.en: There is a problem with the system.

lessons.title: Correct an outdated brochure
lessons.objective: Correct an outdated brochure: Spanish actual usually means current, not the English word actual.

words.es: El horario actual aparece en este documento.
words.en: The current schedule appears in this document.

words.es: Actualmente la oficina abre a las nueve.
words.en: Currently the office opens at nine.

words.es: Pregunto si el precio de la oferta es real.
words.en: I ask whether the offer's price is real.

words.es: La persona confirma que el descuento es verdadero.
words.en: The person confirms that the discount is genuine.

words.es: El documento anterior muestra otro horario.
words.en: The previous document shows a different schedule.

words.es: Uso el horario actual para planear la visita.
words.en: I use the current schedule to plan the visit.

words.es: Un cliente llega con un folleto de la versión anterior.
words.en: A customer arrives with a brochure from the previous version.

words.es: Le explico que el horario actual no es el del folleto.
words.en: I explain that the current schedule is not the one in the brochure.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing correct an outdated brochure. Spanish actual usually means current, not the English word actual. Use real or verdadero for actual in the sense of genuine; actualmente means currently. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Spanish actual usually means current, not the English word actual. Use real or verdadero for actual in the sense of genuine; actualmente means currently.

examples.es: El horario actual aparece en este documento.
examples.en: The current schedule appears in this document.

examples.es: Actualmente la oficina abre a las nueve.
examples.en: Currently the office opens at nine.

lessons.title: Resolve an attendance and service conflict
lessons.objective: Resolve an attendance and service conflict: Asistir a an event means to attend it.
lessons.focus: Resolve an attendance and service conflict

words.en: to attend or assist, depending on context

words.es: Quiero asistir a la reunión del barrio.
words.en: I want to attend the neighborhood meeting.

words.es: Antes del evento tengo que atender a un cliente.
words.en: Before the event I have to help a customer.

words.es: Una compañera puede ayudar con la entrada.
words.en: A colleague can help with the entrance.

words.es: El cliente pregunta cómo participar en la reunión.
words.en: The customer asks how to participate in the meeting.

words.es: Le explico la hora y el lugar del evento.
words.en: I explain the event's time and place to him.

words.es: Tengo un compromiso con el cliente durante el primer turno.
words.en: I have a commitment to the customer during the first shift.

words.es: Busco una solución para poder asistir al evento.
words.en: I look for a solution so I can attend the event.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing resolve an attendance and service conflict. Asistir a an event means to attend it. Atender can mean to help or serve someone; asistir also has a help sense in other contexts. Learn the whole phrase. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Asistir a an event means to attend it. Atender can mean to help or serve someone; asistir also has a help sense in other contexts. Learn the whole phrase.

examples.es: Quiero asistir a la reunión del barrio.
examples.en: I want to attend the neighborhood meeting.

examples.es: Antes del evento tengo que atender a un cliente.
examples.en: Before the event I have to help a customer.

lessons.title: Repair a false-friend misunderstanding
lessons.objective: Repair a false-friend misunderstanding: In ordinary conversation, estar embarazada is normally understood as being pregnant.

words.es: Una amiga está embarazada y comparte la noticia.
words.en: A friend is pregnant and shares the news.

words.es: Yo siento vergüenza por un error en mi mensaje.
words.en: I feel embarrassed about an error in my message.

words.es: La palabra equivocada causa una confusión.
Pido una explicación del significado correcto.
words.en: I ask for an explanation of the correct meaning.

words.es: Mi amiga comprende el error y responde con calma.
words.en: My friend understands the error and responds calmly.

words.es: Corrijo el mensaje antes de enviarlo otra vez.
words.en: I correct the message before sending it again.

words.es: Mi mensaje necesita una disculpa por la confusión.
words.en: My message needs an apology for the confusion.

words.es: Explico mi intención sin repetir el mismo error.
words.en: I explain my intention without repeating the same error.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing repair a false-friend misunderstanding. In ordinary conversation, estar embarazada is normally understood as being pregnant. For embarrassment, prefer tener vergüenza or sentirse avergonzado; other dictionary senses exist, so context still matters. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: In ordinary conversation, estar embarazada is normally understood as being pregnant. For embarrassment, prefer tener vergüenza or sentirse avergonzado; other dictionary senses exist, so context still matters.

examples.es: Una amiga está embarazada y comparte la noticia.
examples.en: A friend is pregnant and shares the news.

examples.es: Yo siento vergüenza por un error en mi mensaje.
examples.en: I feel embarrassed about an error in my message.

lessons.title: Edit a success story accurately
lessons.objective: Edit a success story accurately: Éxito means success; a suceso is an event or occurrence.

words.es: El periódico publica una noticia sobre nuestro proyecto.
words.en: The newspaper publishes a news item about our project.

words.es: El resultado positivo es un éxito para el equipo.
words.en: The positive result is a success for the team.

words.es: Otro artículo describe un suceso en la estación.
words.en: Another article describes an event at the station.
It is not the same news item.

words.es: Preparamos una celebración pequeña para el equipo.
words.en: We prepare a small celebration for the team.

words.es: Explicamos por qué el proyecto tuvo éxito.
words.en: We explain why the project succeeded.

words.es: El artículo incluye una entrevista con el equipo.
words.en: The article includes an interview with the team.

words.es: Un lector no entiende por qué el titular habla de un suceso.
words.en: A reader does not understand why the headline refers to an event.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing edit a success story accurately. Éxito means success; a suceso is an event or occurrence. English success is not normally translated as suceso. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Éxito means success; a suceso is an event or occurrence. English success is not normally translated as suceso.

examples.es: El periódico publica una noticia sobre nuestro proyecto.
examples.en: The newspaper publishes a news item about our project.

examples.es: El resultado positivo es un éxito para el equipo.
examples.en: The positive result is a success for the team.

lessons.title: Check an office inventory without false friends

lessons.focus: Check an office inventory without false friends

words.es: En la oficina hay una alfombra junto a la entrada.
words.en: In the office there is a rug beside the entrance.

words.es: El archivo digital contiene un plano del edificio.
words.en: The digital file contains a plan of the building.

words.es: Pongo la carpeta sobre la mesa.
words.en: I put the folder on the table.

words.es: Una persona comprueba los documentos antes de la visita.
words.en: A person checks the documents before the visit.

words.es: Al salir, recojo mi carpeta y cierro la puerta.

words.es: El inventario incluye una carpeta azul y una alfombra pequeña.

Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Carpeta usually means folder; fábrica means factory. For a carpet, learn alfombra. A familiar spelling is not enough to choose the right object.

lessons.title: Give sensitive and sensible feedback
lessons.objective: Give sensitive and sensible feedback: Sensible often means sensitive; sensato means sensible in the sense of showing good judgment.

words.es: Mi hermano es sensible a ciertos comentarios.
words.en: My brother is sensitive to certain comments.

words.es: Propone un plan sensato para resolver el problema.
words.en: He proposes a sensible plan to solve the problem.

words.es: Una persona escucha su opinión con respeto.
words.en: A person listens to his opinion respectfully.

words.es: El comentario no describe una mala decisión.
words.en: The comment does not describe a bad decision.

words.es: Buscamos una solución que todos puedan aceptar.
words.en: We look for a solution that everyone can accept.

words.es: Antes de responder, explico qué significa sensible.
words.en: Before answering, I explain what sensible means.

words.es: El equipo compara una propuesta nueva con el plan anterior.
words.en: The team compares a new proposal with the previous plan.

words.es: Mi intención es explicar una reacción sin juzgar a la persona.
